record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the precise relationship between the semantic lambda-calculus system Duce and the local π-calculus system π? In particular, can one give a type-preserving encoding of Duce into π that preserves the subtyping relation and correctly handles overloaded functions, recursive types, and the channel type gap chλ(t) versus ch−(t), or do the obstacles encountered indicate a deeper mismatch that instead calls for an integrated concurrent version of Duce?

evidence.quote: There exist several encodings of the λ-calculus into the π-calculus ..., so it seems interesting to study whether the encoding of Duce into π is also possible.

Is this yet another characterisation of some limits of the approach? Does it just mean that Milner’s translation is unfit to model overloading? Or does it instead suggest that the encoding of Duce into π has not a lot of sense and that we had better study how to integrate Duce and π in order to define a concurrent version of Duce?

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question about whether a faithful, subtyping- and type-preserving encoding of the semantic λ-calculus Duce into the local π-calculus exists, or whether the obstacles instead motivate an integrated concurrent Duce. No published resolution was located; later work on semantic subtyping for π-calculi (e.g., Castagna–De Nicola–Varacca and CDuce-related developments) discusses semantic subtyping for processes but does not appear to provide a complete encoding meeting all the stated requirements.
